title: Compute surface phase diagram curves
action: Using the linearized RFA secular equation for the semi-infinite Ising model, compute the reduced surface critical temperature t_c = T_c^s / T_c^b as a function of the surface coupling enhancement Δ_S. Fix Δ_1 = 0 and D_1 = 0 for all curves. Produce two curves: (i) a pure surface with D_S = 0, and (ii) an amorphized surface with D_S = 2.0. For each Δ_S from -1.0 to 5.0 in steps of 0.1, find the physical root t_c ∈ [0,1] of the secular equation and write the results to a CSV.
description: Phase diagram curves showing the surface ordering temperature relative to the bulk Curie temperature versus surface enhancement Δ_S for a pure surface and an amorphized surface.
output_schema: CSV table with columns: Delta_S (float, dimensionless enhancement), t_c (float, reduced critical temperature in [0,1]), param_label (string, 'pure' or 'amorphized').

title: Compute critical surface enhancement Δ_S^c
action: For each surface amorphization parameter D_S in the set [0.0, 0.5, 1.0, ..., 5.0] (step 0.5), with Δ_1 = 0 and D_1 = 0, solve the linearized RFA secular equation for the value of Δ_S that gives t_c = 1 (i.e., the surface orders exactly at the bulk Curie temperature). Write the resulting D_S and critical Δ_S^c to a CSV.
description: Critical surface enhancement Δ_S^c as a function of surface amorphization D_S; the threshold where surface and bulk order simultaneously.
output_schema: CSV table with columns: D_S (float, amorphization parameter from 0.0 to 5.0 step 0.5), Delta_c_S (float, critical enhancement).

title: Compute re-entrant phenomenon curve
action: Compute the surface ordering temperature t_c as a function of the surface structural fluctuation parameter δ_S (defined as δ_S = D_S / (1+Δ_S)). Use fixed parameters Δ_S = 7.0, Δ_1 = -0.9, D_1 = 0. For δ_S from 0.0 to 1.0 in steps of 0.05, solve the secular equation (expressed in terms of δ_S) for the physical root t_c ∈ [0,1]. Write the results to a CSV.
description: Re-entrant phenomenon curve showing surface ordering temperature versus δ_S for a representative parameter set (Δ_S = 7.0, Δ_1 = -0.9), demonstrating how surface fluctuations can destroy surface order.
output_schema: CSV table with columns: delta_S (float, structural fluctuation parameter from 0.0 to 1.0 step 0.05), t_c (float, reduced critical temperature in [0,1]).
